arm_baseline_validity.criterion: signal_to_noise >= 2.0: the sd of scenario means must be at least twice the mean within-scenario sd (seed noise)
arm_baseline_validity.reading: An arm listed in `arms_not_discriminating` cannot be used as evidence that a policy is better or worse: any arm-to-arm difference is measured against a baseline whose outcome is dominated by its own seed noise. Report the arm contrast as 'difference from arm <name> as implemented', never as 'the LLM policy outperforms rule-based management'.

denominator_dependence.primary_reported_above: base-denominated (r_struct divides by the initial LCC)
denominator_dependence.reading: Three numbers answer three different questions and only one survives the cross-subnet comparison. base-denominated: which subnet keeps its largest component under attack -- dominated by how fragmented the subnet starts. n-denominated: how much of the subnet stays connected -- dominated by size and density (AI is ~20x denser). null-relative excess: does targeting beat degree-preserving rewiring of the SAME subnet -- denominator-free. Any prose comparing the subnets on R_struct alone is reporting a normalisation choice.

paired_across_attacks.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank across the attack rankings (n=4; method=exact; very low power)
paired_across_attacks.caveat: n=4 attacks are not independent measures of the same quantity. The exact signed-rank p-value has a floor of 2/2^n = 0.125, which is above 0.05: this test CANNOT reach alpha=0.05 for any outcome. It is descriptive only; the primary RQ1 evidence is the size-matched bootstrap, and a non-significant p here must never be written as 'no difference'.

cross_subnet_comparability.consequence: R_struct per attack is reported as a WITHIN-SUBNET descriptive only; the AI-vs-traditional contrast is NOT_ESTIMABLE under either denominator and must not be quoted as a resilience difference.
cross_subnet_comparability.measured_reason: AI: 19 components, largest 6 of 56 nodes (10.7%), density 0.02468; traditional: 264 components, largest 1116 of 1973 nodes (56.6%), density 0.00116

size_matched_bootstrap.se_definition: sd across bootstrap replicate MEANS = bootstrap SE of the estimate; NOT width/3.92
size_matched_bootstrap.ci95_kind: percentile interval over a bootstrap distribution of the estimator -- an interval for the mean difference, not for a single resample
size_matched_bootstrap.resampling_unit: subnet nodes (size-matched resample); degree-attack AUC only
size_matched_bootstrap.caveat: NOT a graph-level bootstrap, and NOT a subnet-resilience contrast even at the node level: equal n does not give equal m. Read the induced edge counts in `size_matching` before interpreting this difference.

tost_diagnostics.note: a percentile bootstrap interval need not be centred on the mean; when the two SE estimates disagree, width/3.92 UNDERSTATES the SE here, and the stored replicate sd is the one used in the TOST (D-95)

tost.se_source: sd across bootstrap replicate means (stored by s3_resilience)
tost.bootstrap_unit: subnet nodes (size-matched resample); degree-attack AUC only

rq1.metric_note: R_struct = mean AUC, BASE-denominated (initial LCC = 1.0); per-attack AUCs reported separately (P1-2). Read it beside `denominator_dependence` and `cross_subnet_comparability`: the same data gives a different sign under the n-denomination.

rq2.fidelity_reason: point estimate 0.740 >= 0.7 but the 95% interval [0.675, 0.796] crosses the threshold: not established at n=200. H2 fidelity is reported as UNRESOLVED, not as NON_FAITHFUL -- the data cannot separate the two.

ruler_effect_vs_main.reading_t_rec_km: t_rec_km is an exact 0.0 with a zero-width interval here, and NOT_ESTIMABLE in the A2/A3 dose table. Both are statements about different samples, not a contradiction: at A1 no node is removed, so recovery is observable and every pair of runs has the same KM median (an order cannot move a quantity it does not touch); at A2/A3 every run is censored, so no KM median exists and nothing can be compared. Read the zero width as the ABSENCE of variation, never as precision (D-99; cf. rq3.zero_width_reading).

sensitivity.reporting_rule: status=ORDER_CONSISTENT requires identical effect signs across all four Top-k orders AND an order band excluding 0, for every metric and level; otherwise ORDER_DEPENDENT and only the band may be reported

metric_defs.retention_post: per-seed retention at the last turn; dose D = median of paired per-seed differences
metric_defs.r_comp: composite R per seed using the same pre-registered weights and the A-level R_struct
metric_defs.t_rec_km: Kaplan-Meier median of t_rec with censoring; dose D = difference of KM medians (paired bootstrap over seed indices); a censored run is never given a numeric value

sensitivity.pooling: never averaged into the composite R and never entered into the RQ3 ranking

order_overlap_pairwise.note: Per-level pairwise overlap of the removal sets. Orders that overlap heavily are not independent voters: agreement between them repeats one piece of evidence. Read `signs_identical` together with `mean_frac`.

bh_primary.definition: primary = the pre-registered endpoints that carry a p-value (rq2_t_rec via log-rank, rq2_retention_post via Mann-Whitney); exploratory = everything else that carries a p-value (edge_jaccard, substitution_ratio, r_dyn, the RQ1 across-attack paired test). rq1_per_attack_auc_diff is reported per attack with a CI and no multiplicity claim; rq3_composite_r is a 63-scenario ranking and is descriptive, not a test family.

bh_exploratory.definition: primary = the pre-registered endpoints that carry a p-value (rq2_t_rec via log-rank, rq2_retention_post via Mann-Whitney); exploratory = everything else that carries a p-value (edge_jaccard, substitution_ratio, r_dyn, the RQ1 across-attack paired test). rq1_per_attack_auc_diff is reported per attack with a CI and no multiplicity claim; rq3_composite_r is a 63-scenario ranking and is descriptive, not a test family.

faithfulness_gate.reading: rq2 status is FIDELITY_UNRESOLVED, so `rq2_bh` is NOT_ESTIMABLE while `bh_primary` / `bh_exploratory` still print p and q. Those q values are NOT confirmatory: they are computed because the family DEFINITION is what is being audited (D-50), and a q is a statement about a test whose input (the live-vs-lookup policy agreement) has not passed its own faithfulness gate. Quote `rq2_bh.status` as the authoritative verdict on RQ2 and treat every q in the other two families as a description of a family, not as evidence about a policy.

bh_family_note: `rq2_bh` is the family as it was first implemented (all four RQ2 metrics); `bh_primary` / `bh_exploratory` are the families implied by config.simulation.primary_endpoints. They are reported together so that a reader can see the effect of the family definition instead of having to trust one of them (D-50). NOTE the size the primary family actually has: it contains only the pre-registered endpoints that carry a p-value, which is 2. Benjamini-Hochberg on two tests barely corrects (q_max/q_min <= 2 in the worst case and usually far less), so the primary family's control is weak in absolute terms, and `bh_primary.n_tests` / `bh_primary.no_correction` in this file are the authoritative statement of how many tests were corrected -- not this note. `rq1_per_attack_auc_diff` and `rq3_composite_r` belong to no family: the first is per-attack with a CI, the second is a descriptive 63-scenario ranking. Do not attach multiplicity claims to either.
